newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe share index rises on blue chip demand.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe share index rises on blue chip demand.

text.p: Zimbabwe's key industrial index recorded its first gain in a week on Wednesday and only its second this month when it rose nearly 16 points on the back of "limited to reasonable" demand for some bluechips, brokers said.

But they said although the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange (ZSE) had been generally firm and active on the day, the short-term outlook remained mixed-to-soft as investors were still awaiting some new issues on the market.
"Until these are out of the way, gains will be exceptions," one broker commented.

The ZSE's main industrial index closed Wednesday 15.95 points higher at 10,306.98 following some "limited but reasonable demand" for heavyweights such as banking group Barclays, where some 20,600 shares were traded 50 cents higher at 3,450.
Investment, construction and plastic-manufacturing group International Holdings Limited also gained, trading 450 cents up at 2,350.
Some 152,734 shares of coal producer Wankie, which dominates Zimbabwe's mining portfolio, changed hands 10 cents lower each at 500.
And the secondary seven-share mining index dropped 56.44 points to end Wednesday at 939.24 largely on Wankie's account.
